narrative: Material PL1__ME16AB86 displays a clearly intermittent demand pattern — nearly half of all working days record zero consumption, while active days show large, batched withdrawals producing a CV of 1.39. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.37, range 1.06–4.23 days) and contribute only 16.8% of total buffer risk; demand variability dominates at 83.2%. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy is selected: the reorder point of 722 units triggers a fixed replenishment of 824 units (EOQ-optimal, well above MOQ=220), and a safety stock of 433 units is required to maintain the 95% service level target against the high demand uncertainty.
warnings: SAP safety stock (69 units) is critically below the statistically required level (433 units) for 95% service level — stockout risk is high under current policy.
2 upper-tail outliers winsorised at 598.166 units to prevent distortion of standard deviation estimates.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The intermittent but non-negligible demand (48.6% active days, mean 104 units/day) combined with moderate lead time variability suits a continuous-review (r,Q) model. The fixed-order-quantity structure exploits the EOQ cost optimum while the reorder point provides a statistically grounded buffer. Periodic review would add unnecessary exposure during the variable lead times.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (1,891 units) is not binding: safety_stock + order_quantity = 1,257 units leaves 634 units of headroom. No capacity-driven service degradation expected.
